claims.text: At stage-1 DonHang.App writes its text into widgets, such as const Text('Sign in') in LoginScreen and Text('No products yet.') in ProductListScreen, while MaterialApp's title is 'Đơn Hàng' and ProductTile shows the price followed by 'đ'.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: login_screen.dart:44,60; product_list_screen.dart:54; main.dart:19; widgets/product_tile.dart:29

claims.text: l10n.yaml sets arb-dir: lib/l10n and template-arb-file: app_en.arb; app_en.arb and app_vi.arb map the same keys to English and Vietnamese text (e.g. signIn: 'Sign in' / 'Đăng nhập', noProducts: 'Chưa có sản phẩm nào.'), appTitle is 'Đơn Hàng' in both.

gen-l10n reads the ARB files in arb-dir and generates an AppLocalizations class with one getter per message key (e.g. String get signIn); the template ARB file declares the keys the other ARB files translate.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: Internationalizing Flutter apps (gen-l10n, l10n.yaml options arb-dir, template-arb-file); generated lib/l10n/app_localizations.dart @ stage-2

claims.text: Using a key that is not in the ARB files, e.g. l10n.signin, is a compile error: flutter analyze reports undefined_getter for AppLocalizations.
claims.source_hint: generator check: flutter analyze on stage-2 archive with AppLocalizations.of(context).signin -> error undefined_getter; Dart language: undefined getter is a static error

claims.text: AppLocalizations.localizationsDelegates holds the app's own delegate plus the Global Material/Cupertino/Widgets delegates; supportedLocales is [Locale('en'), Locale('vi')], one per ARB file, in alphabetical order (gen-l10n's default), so en is first.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: lib/l10n/app_localizations.dart; flutter_tools gen_l10n.dart (allLocales..sort(), preferredSupportedLocales doc)

claims.text: MaterialApp compares the platform's preferred locales (on the web, the browser's preferred languages), in order, with supportedLocales and picks the closest match; with vi first it picks vi; with no match it uses the first entry of supportedLocales.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: basicLocaleListResolution; docs: Internationalizing Flutter apps; probe on stage-2 archive: [vi_VN]->vi, [fr_FR]->en, [fr_FR,vi]->vi, [ja,de]->en

claims.text: AppLocalizations.of(context) returns Localizations.of<AppLocalizations>(context, AppLocalizations): it looks up the tree from the widget's context for the messages loaded for the current locale; with nullable-getter: false it returns a non-null value.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: lib/l10n/app_localizations.dart (static of), l10n.yaml:8-9; Flutter API: Localizations.of

claims.text: In an ARB file, @@locale names the file's language, and an entry whose key starts with @ (such as @appTitle) is not a message but describes the message with the same name, here with a description.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: Internationalizing Flutter apps (ARB format, @ resource attributes, description); ARB specification; app_en.arb:2-4 @ stage-2

claims.text: onGenerateTitle receives a context that includes the app's Localizations, so it can call AppLocalizations.of(context); at stage-1 main.dart used the fixed title: 'Đơn Hàng'.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: MaterialApp.onGenerateTitle / WidgetsApp.onGenerateTitle ('context includes the WidgetsApp's Localizations widget'); main.dart:30 @ stage-2, main.dart:19 @ stage-1

claims.text: At stage-2 every screen's build starts with final l10n = AppLocalizations.of(context) (or calls AppLocalizations.of(context) directly), and no file in DonHang.App/lib passes a string literal to Text.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: git grep "Text('" -- DonHang.App/lib (no match); screens/*.dart, widgets/product_tile.dart

claims.text: Every ARB file is compiled into the app (one generated class per language), and the locale is chosen from the browser's preferred languages while the app runs, so one build shows Vietnamese or English depending on the browser.
claims.source_hint: generated app_localizations_en.dart / app_localizations_vi.dart @ stage-2; generator check: headless Chrome --accept-lang=vi / en / fr on the lab's localhost:8081 (same build, vi and en text)

claims.text: localhost:8081/login shows LoginScreen whether or not the user signed in (the redirect only guards /orders): title 'Sign in', button 'Sign in with Keycloak' with English first in Chrome's preferred languages; 'Đăng nhập', 'Đăng nhập bằng Keycloak' with Vietnamese first; English with French only.
claims.source_hint: generator check: headless Chrome on the lab's localhost:8081/login with --accept-lang=en, vi, fr; router.dart redirect @ stage-2; app_en.arb/app_vi.arb

claims.text: A widget that reads its text by key needs only one layout for all languages; a copy of each screen per language would double every later fix.
